title: Distemper Outbreak Halts Dog Adoptions at Oklahoma City Shelter: What Frenchie Owners Should Check
seoTitle: Distemper Outbreak at OKC Shelter: What to Check
description: Canine distemper at Oklahoma City's animal shelter paused dog adoptions on Nov 19, 2026. Signs to watch, and what French Bulldog owners should check before boarding.

faq.q: Why did the Oklahoma City shelter stop dog adoptions?
faq.a: Oklahoma City Animal Welfare paused dog adoptions and routine dog intakes on November 19, 2026, after five shelter dogs tested positive for canine distemper. Three of them were euthanized because of symptoms.

faq.q: How long will dog adoptions be suspended?
faq.a: At least two weeks. The shelter said adoptions resume when the virus is no longer present in the shelter population; no exact date was given.

faq.q: Is there a distemper outbreak across Oklahoma City?
faq.a: The cases reported so far are inside the shelter. The reports do not describe cases elsewhere in the city.

faq.q: Can cats catch canine distemper from shelter dogs?
faq.a: The shelter says domestic cats are not susceptible, so cat adoptions continue. Veterinary references list large wild cats among species the virus can infect.

faq.q: Are French Bulldogs at higher risk of distemper?
faq.a: Nothing in the reports suggests that. Vaccination is available and generally effective for all dogs; ask your vet whether your Frenchie's distemper vaccine is current.
